title: The Defilement of the Sanctuary and the Scattering of the Apostles
english: His throne lasts until the passing of the heavens, but like the days of heaven; for after the passing, heaven is. It is not possible for its passing to be perishable. And The bright and vigorous things can be days of the earth, but the bright and luminous mysteries of truth are days of heaven;ewise, the throne of the Savior, having been placed unshakable, remains forever.

In this, God steadfastly promises by swearing, upon which He has spoken and enters into (Ps 88:36–38). Since He does not change His mind after swearing, giving an unpassable priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek, He remains constant; and having promised to Abraham with an oath that in his seed all the nations of the earth would be blessed, He shows the immovability of the blessing. If indeed He gives something by chance, He does not swear upon it; for indeed, having given the kingdom to Saul without an oath, He did not change His mind. Since He also willed that the Savior be born from David according to the flesh, and that his seed, having come from David, be unpassable and steadfast, He was faithful to Him regarding the making of the unshakable promises. Therefore, O Moses, David [says]: 'In my holiness, not lying, upon which I promised, his seed remains for ever, sharing the throne of his beginning with the Sun of Righteousness.' And the moon remains most fully illuminated as the gathering of those being enlightened by Christ for ever, when the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the righteous shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Ps 88:39–46). And a faithful witness concerning this being so in the heavens exists; concerning Job he says, 'Behold, in the heavens is my witness and my supporter in the highest' (Job 16:19).

But Didymus did not give the intellect in the same way as the interpretation of Eusebius: 'You, O Lord, having said the seed of Christ remains for ever, have cast away his seed.' Having rendered him powerless, taking up the Christ, who, having been anointed with holy oil, remains for ever and ever, those descending from him shall be shown mercy. Having overthrown the covenant of your servant, having cast up the Christ, though having said you would not profane your covenant with him.

And having defiled even his sanctuary into the earth, indeed his body is given unto death and a memory, while the church, being near, and his sanctuary having been defiled into that earth in the times during which you permitted or continued persecutions to be accomplished for the sake of the godless.

But Christ, the servant of God, is found having taken the form of a servant, becoming according to what was said to the angel, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord, let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38). And you demolished all his enclosures from his sons, every most fortified help, so that those attempting to plot against them might be able to act against them. For enclosures, according to the Scripture, are diversely becoming guards from God; and it is possible to call the apostles the enclosures of the Christ's vineyard, whom those seeing them scattered say are being removed by God, having been scandalized in the night of the betrayal of Jesus (Matt 26:56). You reproached his strongholds with cowardice. It has been said that the true disciples of Christ are his strongholds, having been placed in cowardice at the time of the betrayal of Jesus.

It followed that Christ was snatched away by those pursuing or departing from the way. But Christ, being snatched away, is not another from those snatching away his body; for you are the body of Christ and members in part (1 Cor 12:27). And it is possible also to call the strongholds of his church according to various local dwellings his strongholds.

To this also you reproach him toward those called his neighbors because of being toward him and around him. For those who seem to be gathered as neighbors of him through a pseudonymous knowledge, thinking that they contain his Scripture and are near his church, are those through whom they think and act badly, reproaching him. For just as he who works rightly and praises rightly according to the truth glorifies him from the opposite, so those who are disposed oppositely to the right ones reproach him. Because of these things, you reproached him on the right side of his enemies; for they exult as if they had overcome by their own power, and having done so, you abandoned him. title: The meaning of 'Who'
english: The sword of his help; for it is carried on both sides. For having gone to war against Christ, his enemies, and hating him, they did not stand against him in the war, as if they had decided to lead him away to be crucified and to bring all other things against him insultingly.

These things will cease from saying, those who have desire toward Christ and having rightly received the providence, not seeing the intention according to which the Father, not sparing his own Son, delivered him to those standing and gathered against him, having learned the salvation having been made straight through his death, not only of the Father having delivered him on behalf of us but also of himself having delivered himself unto this; for he gave his soul a ransom for many.

Having removed the debt through his cleansing, and the following things as of the psalm. Thinking that he had departed from the things promised to him, and they say these things. For they supposed him to be abolished from the cleansing, [thinking] he did not work through his blood; upon which they think also that his throne has been broken down to the earth, the days of his throne being shortened.

But nothing of this sort will happen concerning his throne, since God has established him as the days of heaven, not as the things that are earthly. But also God remains in opposition to himself if the throne of Christ is as the sun and the completed moon for the age. For having seen him having been crucified and having suffered, they saw him having received the kingdom at the end, his throne having been diminished and overturned, and having taken upon himself the shame upon the cross, concerning which the apostle says: He endured the cross, despising the shame, instead of the joy set before him, having risen from the dead, no longer being abolished by the cleansing but perfecting and working, him removing the sin of the world, according to the said thing: having made a cleansing of sins, he sat at the right hand of majesty in the high places, being raised up and having firmly established the throne, remaining for a long time and an eternal age (Ps 88:47-48a).

Remember, we who are saying these things, what the substance is. For we are unstable and changeable being autonomous; therefore also we fear lest we be drawn into impiety. O God, looking quickly upon your mercy...

For the expressed anger is not of such a nature as to be merely extinguished. The term 'hypostasis' may not signify the essence, as we have interpreted, but rather that which one is able to sustain according to the underlying state.

Since 'who' signifies many things, let us observe what is meant by the various uses of 'Who is man?'. For 'who' sometimes signifies a person, as in 'Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord, and who shall stand in his holy place?' (Ps 24:3). It also denotes the rare or exceptional, as in 'Who is the faithful and prudent servant?' and 'Who is wise and understands these things?' and 'Who is discerning and will know these?'. The word is even applied to the incapable in 'Who knows the Lord?' and 'Who became his counselor?' and 'Who gathered the winds in his bosom?' and 'Who turned the water into a garment?'. The word is also applied to the insignificant, as if he were no one, in 'If God is for us, who is against us?' (Rom 8:31) and 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who will harm me?' (Ps 118:7). It is also applied to one called by a specific name by some, but by others as an individual or a single unit, as in 'a certain noble man'.

Here it is possible to grasp the upcoming passage regarding 'no one': 'For who is the man that shall live and not see death?' (Ps 39:5) instead of 'No one'. And if the discourse is about common death, no one truly lives and does not see death, according to what is said, 'For death passed upon all men, of whom all sinned' (Rom 5:12), and 'For it is appointed unto men once to die' (Heb 9:27). For 'who' is equivalent to 'all men'. No one is a man, since every man is a mortal creature, and every man having fallen from divinity, as in 'You die as men' and 'Wherefore your wrath and indignation, are ye not as men and walk after the manner of men?'. For none of such people have become unhistorical regarding death by sinning; therefore it is said, 'Who is the man that shall live?'. For such a thing is a god, among those called gods through participation in divinity. For they alone shall not see death, since they live by transforming into eternal life; a life which Hades shall not be able to consume or hold, as God saves such people from the hand of Hades.

title: The fulfillment of prophecy and the light of mercy
english: He says that those seated with the apostles, the earth being shaped to be a soul capable of bearing fruit, and the inhabited world in which angels dwell, and the dogmas of truth and the gifts of the Spirit, will speak before all these, just as to the prophets God has become a refuge from generation to generation. And the phrase 'And from the age and as of the age you are' signifies the movement of God from infinity to infinity. For you are the same one remaining forever, not one in one age and another in another age; for you are the same one, unchangeable and immutable, from infinity to infinity.

Having raised man from things of lowliness and debasement to height, guarding him in that suspension and height, do not turn him back to become such as the low things (Ps 89:3). Place our iniquities before you, to punish us for them, as all our age—and time is that which extends our day with bodily life—is manifest and enlightened to you, not only of every transgression in practice but also of that which is manifest and enlightened to you in thoughts (Ps 89:8).

The coming prayer of those standing by is: what God has in his right hand, and to see it, what they are doing (Ps 89:12-17). As those standing say: O Lord God, reveal the providence of the world which you created through your right hand, so that we may grasp not how it does and works through it, but let us know it as it approaches us. The petition of those calling upon the presence of Christ is able, for He himself is the right hand of God. For then the right hand of God became known, who is the Word having become flesh who dwelt among us; for we beheld his glory as of the only-begotten from the Father. And having known the right hand of God, let us know with it those who have been instructed in wisdom in the heart, who are not merely those who claim to be. But we speak of Wisdom in the perfect ones. It is possible even for the prophets to be known as those having been instructed in wisdom in the heart, for whom the brightness of Christ has been revealed. For then the prophets, truly proclaiming beforehand concerning him, were shown to be perhaps able.
Before their prophecies were fulfilled. For their words have reached an outcome through the revealed right hand of God, and they have become manifest as if they were instructed by the wisdom of God.

But the heart is instructed in wisdom by one who has made the mind and the ruling principle wise, as the speaker himself contends in ten thousand ways as if to say they are speaking truly: 'Even if [he is] an unlearned man in speech, yet not in knowledge.' And it is also said, 'Those laid low in heart by wisdom.' For the thought and the memory are laid low from the plains of the wisdom of the wise and the pious one imposing [it] upon things; and it is said concerning the plains of wisdom, that we protect the feet of the soul by stepping into them.

'Turn back, O Lord; how long will you turn your face and your right hand away from us?' (Ps 30:16). For you do this to us for only a little while, yet a long time appears to those exhausted by the longing. Having been discouraged among your servants, turn back to us, having become distant and having turned away from your commands.

'We have been filled in the morning with your mercy' (Ps 89:13). For your right hand, which we were worthy to be made known, having shone upon us, prepared the beginning of a spiritual day, like the sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2). In the beginning, occurring in the morning, we were filled with the mercy from you, as your true light enlightened us in all those days so that we might rejoice and be glad (Ps 119:130). It is not something entering into our minds in the morning that is poetic.

But since it rises to us not in one way but diversely according to various actions and thoughts, we come to be [filled] in many days; in all those [days] let us rejoice and be glad, so much as to be able to loose the dark and evil exterior of the days, in which you humbled us by captivity and delivered us to enemies through ignorance and malice. For in days and in many more, having been humbled, we see evils, but you [provide] the opposites of the truly good things, concerning which it is said, 'The fool does evil in jest,' or the things that are burdensome and causing harm, concerning which it is said to Job, 'If we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not also receive evil?'
